projects.title: Modeling the Male Adult Nerve Cord of The Drosophila Melanogaster Using Spiking Neural Networks
projects.description: Recent literature in the field of neuronal locomotion has been able to successfully map the ventral nerve cord (VNC) of the male Drosophila Melanogaster in a public data set that offers a robust connectome of the VNC. This research project seeks to model the data found in the Male Adult Nerve Cord (MANC), utilizing a differential equation-based, spiking neural network model (SNNs). With over 23,000 neurons, this model is based on the leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) that is used to simulate neurons due to its biological realism and computational efficiency. By having a full data set and mapping the over 5.3 million different synaptic connections, researchers will be able to automate the mapping process of local neuron circuits when they experiment with silencing or simulating certain neurons. This project ultimately aims to create an exploratory tool that will enable researchers to better understand the underlying functional architecture of the MANC. Our model demonstrates the viability of continuing to model the Drosophila's nervous system through the connectivity and predicted neurotransmitter identities of neurons alone, and the ability to yield hypotheses that are experimentally verifiable.

honors_and_awards.title: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship Recipient
honors_and_awards.description: The Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship is an initiative by Amazon aimed at supporting high school seniors in the United States who are pursuing a computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics or related degree. The scholarship provides recipients with $40,000 towards their college tuition and a guaranteed paid internship at Amazon after their first year of college.
